abort.already_configured: Tesla v1r is already configured. To change settings, use the Configure button on the integration card.
abort.monitoring_cleanup_failed: Monitoring Mode was not enabled because Tesla v1r could not safely release its current battery control. Check the logs and try again.
abort.no_energy_sites: No Tesla energy sites found. Ensure you have a Powerwall or Solar system set up in the Tesla app before adding Tesla v1r.
abort.reauth_failed: Re-authentication failed. Remove the integration and set it up again.
abort.reauth_fleet_api_use_tesla_fleet: Tesla v1r reads tokens from your Tesla Fleet integration. Go to Settings > Devices & Services > Tesla Fleet and re-authenticate there. Tesla v1r will pick up the new tokens automatically.
abort.reauth_successful: Token updated -- Tesla v1r is reconnected.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the API server. Check your internet connection and that Home Assistant has outbound HTTPS access.
error.captcha_required: GloBird requested captcha verification. Sign in through the GloBird portal in a browser, then try again.
error.invalid_auth: Token rejected by the API -- check you copied the full token string with no extra spaces.
error.invalid_display_currency: Select Automatic, AUD, EUR, GBP, NZD, or SEK.
error.invalid_flow_power_plan: Choose a Flow Power plan and a region supported by that plan.
error.invalid_globird_auth: Email or password is incorrect. Check your GloBird portal login credentials.
error.invalid_postcode: Enter a valid four-digit Australian postcode.
error.invalid_time: Enter a valid 24-hour time in HH:MM format.
error.no_energy_sites: No Tesla energy sites found. Ensure your Powerwall or Solar system is set up in the Tesla app before continuing.
error.no_sites: No Amber sites found for this token. Verify the token belongs to an account with an active Amber site.
error.no_token_provided: Paste a token in the field above. See the hint text for where to find it.
error.powerwall_gateway_invalid: Enter a bare Powerwall IP/hostname or an HTTP(S) URL without credentials, a path, query, or invalid port.
error.season_month_gap: Tariff seasons must cover all 12 months before continuing.
error.season_month_invalid: Choose valid start and end months for the tariff season.
error.season_month_overlap: Tariff seasons overlap. Each month can belong to only one season.
error.season_name_invalid: Each tariff season needs a unique, non-empty name.
error.season_required: Add at least one tariff season.
error.tesla_fleet_not_installed: Tesla Fleet integration is not installed in Home Assistant. Add it from Settings > Devices & Services > Add Integration > Tesla Fleet, then return here.
error.tesla_force_discharge_prices_invalid: Enter finite Tesla force-discharge prices from $0 to $99/kWh, with the sell price higher than the buy price.
error.unknown: An unexpected error occurred. Check the Home Assistant logs for details and try again.

data_description.battery_management_mode: Manual = Tesla v1r automations control charge/discharge. TOU Sync = prices synced to battery's built-in scheduler. Smart Optimization = LP solver minimises costs.
data_description.optimization_backup_reserve: Intentional battery export stops at this level. Natural self-consumption may continue to the separate hardware backup reserve.

battery_management_mode.description: Choose how Tesla v1r manages your battery.
battery_management_mode.title: Battery management mode

data_description.battery_system: If you have multiple battery brands, choose the primary system that Tesla v1r should control.

battery_system.description: Select the battery or hybrid inverter installed at your site. This determines which connection protocol Tesla v1r uses.
battery_system.title: Battery system

data_description.custom_battery_level_entity: State of charge as a percentage.
data_description.custom_battery_power_entity: Battery power. Positive means discharging; negative means charging.
data_description.custom_grid_power_entity: Grid power. Positive means importing; negative means exporting.
data_description.optimization_allow_grid_charge: When disabled, the planner will not schedule forced grid charging.
data_description.optimization_backup_reserve: The optimizer will never plan discharge below this percentage.
data_description.optimization_battery_capacity_wh: Total usable battery capacity in kWh for the external battery system.
data_description.optimization_max_charge_w: Maximum charge power in kW that the planner may schedule.
data_description.optimization_max_discharge_w: Maximum battery/inverter discharge power in kW that the planner may schedule for loads and export.
data_description.optimization_max_grid_export_w: Site/DNSP export cap in kW. Auto-detected only when your inverter reports its own export limit; otherwise Profit Max solar export stays off until you set this. Set 0 for zero-export sites. This does not limit battery power used by house loads.
data_description.optimization_max_grid_import_w: Maximum site grid import in kW. Set 0 for no site import cap.

custom_battery.description: Select the Home Assistant entities Tesla v1r should use to model your battery system. Tesla v1r will generate optimizer plans in monitoring mode and will not send control commands.
custom_battery.title: Custom external controller

data_description.optimization_provider: Smart Optimization generally delivers lower bills but requires the HiGHS solver (highspy). The native mode is simpler and uses your battery's own scheduling logic.

optimization_provider.description: Choose how Tesla v1r schedules your battery. The built-in option uses your {battery_name}'s native TOU scheduler; Smart Optimization runs a cost-minimising LP solver inside Tesla v1r.
optimization_provider.title: Optimization mode

data_description.electricity_provider: If your retailer is not listed, choose Other / Custom TOU to enter rates manually.

provider_selection.description: Select your electricity retailer. Tesla v1r will fetch pricing and sync it to your battery on a 5-minute cycle.
provider_selection.title: Electricity provider

data_description.amber_forecast_type: Predicted is balanced. Low assumes cheaper prices (more aggressive charging). High assumes expensive prices (more conservative).
data_description.amber_site_id: If you have multiple Amber NMIs, select the one associated with this Powerwall.
data_description.auto_sync_enabled: When enabled, Tesla v1r uploads a new TOU tariff schedule to your battery every 5 minutes based on current Amber prices.
data_description.battery_curtailment_enabled: Stop battery export when earnings fall below the configured threshold. This controls the battery/Tesla path only; supported DC solar curtailment has its own opt-in.
data_description.powerwall_local_ip: Optional. Provides direct LAN access for live local polling and fast gateway writes — pairing handles authentication via RSA signing, no password required.
data_description.tesla_energy_site_id: The Powerwall or Solar site that Tesla v1r will control. If you have multiple Tesla sites, choose the one at this address.

site_selection.description: Match your Tesla energy site with your electricity account. If you only have one of each, they are pre-selected.
site_selection.title: Select your sites

data_description.tesla_api_provider: Controls how Tesla v1r reads and writes your Powerwall TOU schedule. Tesla v1r.cc is free and handles OAuth for you.
data_description.tesla_ev_api_provider: Only needed if you want Tesla v1r to send commands to a Tesla vehicle (e.g. start/stop charging). Choose None if you only have a Powerwall or use BLE.
data_description.tesla_force_discharge_buy_price: Temporary Tesla import price during force discharge. Defaults to $0.55/kWh; this is a control signal, not your retail tariff.
data_description.tesla_force_discharge_sell_price: Temporary Tesla export price during force discharge. Defaults to $25.00/kWh and must exceed the buy price; this is a control signal, not your feed-in tariff.

user.description: Configure Tesla v1r to sync electricity pricing to your battery system automatically.
user.title: Tesla v1r setup

covau_plan_withdrawn.description: AER plan {plan_id} was withdrawn on {withdrawn_date}. Tesla v1r will keep using the cached immutable snapshot and will not move you to a successor automatically. Open Configure > Electricity pricing and confirm the exact plan on your current bill, or enter the validated manual tariff.
covau_plan_withdrawn.title: CovaU SolarMax plan snapshot has been withdrawn

flow_power_web_data_api_required.description: Flow Power has retired automated customer-portal access. Your portal credentials and session cookies were removed. In the Flow Power app, go to **More > Web Data Access**, copy the API key, then open **Settings > Devices & Services > Tesla v1r > Configure > Electricity pricing & provider** and enter it. AEMO-direct pricing continues while the key is missing, but Flow Power API prices and account metrics are unavailable.
flow_power_web_data_api_required.title: Flow Power Web Data API key required

solar_export_limit_not_configured.description: Profit Max can hold battery charging so high-priced solar exports instead, but it needs to know your site export cap first. Your battery connection does not report one, so Tesla v1r cannot auto-detect it. Open **Settings > Devices & Services > Tesla v1r > Configure > Smart Optimization > Grid & site constraints** and set **Maximum grid export** to your site/DNSP export cap in kW (for example 5 for a 5 kW limit). Until then every candidate slot falls back to self-consumption.
solar_export_limit_not_configured.title: Set your maximum grid export for Profit Max solar export
